claim: Theorem 4, case alpha_1 = alpha_2, beta_1 <= beta_2: likelihood ratio part
quote: Let Xi ~ GaL(alpha_i, beta_i), i = 1, 2, be two random variables. If alpha_1 = alpha_2 = alpha and beta_1 <= beta_2, and if beta_1 = beta_2 = beta >= 1 with alpha_1 <= alpha_2, then X1 <lr X2 => X1 <hr X2 => X1 <st X2. ... if alpha_1 = alpha_2 = alpha, then X1 is stochastically smaller than X2 with respect to the likelihood ratio if and only if beta_1 <= beta_2.
model: other: two distributions of the same family
family: GaL (compound gamma-Lindley): pdf proportional to alpha beta^2 (1+alpha+beta+x) x^{alpha-1} e^{-x} / [(1+beta)(beta+x)^{alpha+2}]
compared: X1 ~ GaL(alpha, beta_1) vs X2 ~ GaL(alpha, beta_2), shared alpha

conclusion.direction: X1 <=_lr X2; the proof states 'if and only if beta_1 <= beta_2'

ambiguity: Proved iff: d/dx log g1(x) = q(beta_2) - q(beta_1) < 0 since q decreasing in beta.
